note: CROSS-LANGUAGE CONTRACT. Byte-identical copies live at prappser-spaces/files/reminder_recurrence_fixture.json and prappser-app/test/features/reminder/recurrence_fixture.json; internal/reminder/recurrence_golden_test.go and test/features/reminder/recurrence_golden_test.dart both assert it. dtstart is local wall time in tz (no offset suffix); expected are absolute epoch seconds. Expansion is on LOCAL WALL TIME: a 09:00 reminder stays 09:00 across a DST transition. Two policies are pinned by the dst- cases below and must match in both languages: a NONEXISTENT local time (spring forward) shifts forward by the gap (02:30 -> 03:30 CEST), and an AMBIGUOUS local time (fall back) takes the POST-transition offset (02:30 CET, the second of the two). Values were derived from wall times via system tzdata, independently of both implementations. A divergence is a real finding: do not edit this file to make a test pass.

cases.name: weekly BYDAY=MO UNTIL cuts off the 4th
dst spring-forward: weekly 09:00 keeps wall time across 2026-03-29 (CET->CEST), the 7d step becomes 167h
dst fall-back: weekly 09:00 keeps wall time across 2026-10-25 (CEST->CET), the 7d step becomes 169h
dst nonexistent local time: daily 02:30 hits 2026-03-29 02:30 which does not exist; policy = shift forward by the gap to 03:30 CEST
dst ambiguous local time: daily 02:30 hits 2026-10-25 02:30 which occurs twice; policy = post-transition offset (CET)
